posts.name: Humble-Knight
posts.cooked:
So, on G+ tonight I tried the new promos (sans Cosmic). In general I really liked them. I only got to use Tempest and Haka, but I saw the other 2 played and got to think about how I would have played them.

Haka gets set up really fast this way. We were fighting Voss admittably, but I had every ongoing and equipment card out except Punish the weak, and that was purposeful. He's fun and he combos well with the Tempest. Ultimately, it didn't feel all that different from regular Haka.

I also played Tempest, and while Tempest himself was a beast, several times this power was a lot less useful than his normal one or any of the ones in his deck. Except when I needed to kill something or at the very beginning of the game to set up a bit, I never used this power. His deck doesn't have enough draw to support that power. I used it a couple times to play an extra one shot, and once to get a piece of equipment out, but other than that I just didn't have cards that justified the damage or the cards I would take away from vicious cyclone. I like this power but to me it seems a bit too open. You almost need localized hurricane to use it effectively, and I think that late game as a set up would be great, but early game it seems more useless. 

Adept's power I don't think got used properly so I want to see it again, but in general it's mostly a different way to play him, neither better or worse.

Fanatic's power is great. She gets a lot more one shots out, which boosts her damage a lot, it combos well with sacrosanct martyr, wrathful retribution and zealous offense really well. It also makes her a bit into a support, which is interesting. The randomness is the only draw back, but it's small. The biggest fear is a poor timed end of days, but the likelyhood of that is low.

In general, I like them and want to play with them some more

Captain's is probably the most functional promo yet, it is designed to capitalize on the matches where Captain would normally struggle the most.

Foote wrote:
Argent Adept: So colorful. I'd really like a lore explaination of that art. Idk, but that seems like a straight up better power than Vocalize. Very interesting.  
I can't say it's straight up better. It activates an Accompany Text, something Melodies don't have at all. Then when you look at Accompanies and Performs, Syncopated Onslaught's Accompany is not as good as Scherzo of Frost and Flame's Perform. Alacritious Subdominant's Accompany is not as good as Inspiring Supertonic's Perform. Inventive Preperation's Accompany is not as good as Alacritious Subdominant's Perform. Then the Accompany for Inspiring Supertonic may or may not be better than the Perform on Rhapsody of Vigor, depending on who needs healing. This only leaves Cedistic Dissonant and Counterpoint Bulwark that cannot be replicated as a Perform Text.

It's really no surprise that an activate an accompany power actually gets more text than just a perform. Especially with the ease to possibly not even get a card with an accompany text on it, or having a Polyphoric Flare on bottom, ouch.

There are three of the Argent's songs that have no accompany text, and multiple others where the perform requires you to have a specific instrument.  

With vocalize, you could always rely on being able to do something- not necessarily one of the big chains, but you could always make use of part of each power, since all of them have a perform.  With the new one, you have to be more reliant on the instruments.

posts.name: Reckless
posts.cooked:
I had little issue with Prime Tempest and card draw. Aquatic Correspondence is a beast with his innate, and you can Reclaim from the Deep it. On the turns you need more cards (Through Localized Hurricane or Aquatic Correspondence) you will likely already have access to other cards that either buff his damage, deal damage, or provide DR so your turn isn’t all hand recovery.

I’m not saying he has the best draw, but he can still reliably reuse his draw cards enough to maintain his innate most of the time. It just takes a bit of work.
